additions.reason: Apply the same insulation mechanism to opposite everyday situations; distinguish heat generation from slower transfer.
Distinguish final temperature from change, using explicitly labelled illustrative measurements.
Apply the distinction between a renewable flow and a finite store; request evidence for the water budget.

corrections.change: Solid particles vibrate about fixed positions; they are not motionless. Mobile electrons contribute in metals.
Use expansion and lower density, not an unexplained loss of mass. Cups may respond to draughts or imbalance.
Insulation slows rather than stops transfer; two thin blankets are not unconditionally better than one thick blanket.
Breeze reversal is a typical local pattern, not an everyday guarantee.
Several mechanisms act simultaneously; do not describe the gas-flame-to-pan path solely as conduction or cooling solely as radiation.
Clouds contain condensed droplets/ice, not simply vapour; seasonal snowfall does not necessarily replace all melted glacier ice.
An aquifer stores and transmits water in connected openings. Recharge is finite, can be slow, and is not all infiltrating water.
Historical rainfall methods retained as history, not validated modern forecasting.
No guarantee of supplying water all summer; capacity and weather matter.
Make equal spacing/wax and heat between II/III explicit to resolve the source pin diagram.
Nested tumblers help through trapped air only if leakage/contact does not eliminate the insulating gap.
Make equal starting temperature, water amount and heating time explicit; retain differing heat/bulb positions.
Paper near flames is not an unsupervised learner task. Preserve the question through teacher-controlled demonstration or video; paper can still burn.
